choice.div: "An applicant rejected by the model is not told why and has no appeal; residual risk accepted by [name], reviewed quarterly."

div.p: Harm, affected people, residual risk and a named acceptor make the entry reviewable.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: When is "human in the loop" a real control?

choice.div: When the human has the time, information and authority to disagree.

div.p: A rubber-stamp review is not oversight. The three conditions are what make it real.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Residual risk exceeds your delegated authority. What should happen?

choice.div: Escalate to a person with the authority to accept it, and record the decision.
Accept it and note it later.
Lower the severity score until it fits.

div.p: Acceptance is a decision with a level. Adjusting the score to avoid escalation is falsifying the register.

choiceresponse.p: Which are common false comforts in a risk register? Select all that apply.

choice.div: An average score that hides a severe outcome for a small group.
A review step with no time or authority to disagree.
A vendor certificate treated as absolution.

div.p: Averages, nominal review and certification transfer are false comfort. Named ownership and triggers are real controls.
